page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 16 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with an x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 8 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. The memory configuration provides 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptographic instructions. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-highcpu-16 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 25% on stress-ng single-core tests. Its PassMark memory score also ranks in the top 25%, indicating efficient memory subsystem performance. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. The instance achieves average memory bandwidth, with read-only small block speeds of 1085.32 GB/sec and large block write speeds of 48.72 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning tasks, it registers a strong text generation speed of 301.82 tokens/sec using a small 135M model, though prompt processing remains average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highcpu-16 offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources without massive memory footprints. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly resource-dense for compute-bound tasks. This instance is suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, ray tracing, and moderate database operations.
